headline: Senior Associate, Human Capital Advisory at KPMG US | Management Consultant | Learning & Development
about:
I currently work as a Senior Consultant within the Human Capital Advisory Consulting practice at KPMG US, specializing in designing, developing, and delivering engaging learning solutions to support organizations in large-scale technology implementations while partnering with leaders and key stakeholders to implement change, promote a skills-driven culture, and drive business outcomes. I have worked across a wide array of industries, including healthcare, telecommunications, and state and local government.

Prior to joining KPMG, I worked in corporate human resources functions at Huron Consulting Group and UnitedHealth Group, specializing in new hire onboarding and orientation, employee listening surveys, and talent development initiatives. 

I have a Master's in Human Resources and Industrial Relations (MHRIR) from the University of Illinois at Urbana-Champaign, and a Bachelor of Arts in Advertising & Public Relations from the School of Communication, Loyola University of Chicago, with a concentration in Asian Studies. My skillsets and areas of interest include learning experience, instructional design, new hire onboarding, change management, and employee experience.

headline: Global Trade Transformation Leader at KPMG
about:
I help my clients navigate the immense complexities of global trade, bringing knowledge of best in class trade compliance processes and technologies. I have a passion for Innovation and use technology and cutting edge organizational design tools, to enable global trade transformation to achieve incremental value for multi-national enterprises. 

The views expressed by me are my own and not that of my employer or other party.

experience.description: Leading teams and projects to help my clients innovate and transform their trade compliance processes through cutting edge technologies and organizational design techniques.

Senior Manager with KPMG’s Trade and Customs practice 

I started working with KPMG in the UK, focusing on Customs and other indirect taxes.  During this seven years I specialized in assessing, obtaining and operating duty reliefs for clients.  In addition, I also focused on customs valuation, international VAT and process improvement projects for mutlinational clients across the EU, providing me with a significant cross border EU experience.

Working for KPMG UK allowed me to undertake a full time secondment with KPMG in Hong Kong.  During this time I learned about the Chinese business culture and tax environment and conducted reviews of vendors for first sale implementation.

I relocated to the US in 2007 and have sinced worked on a wide range of customs consulting projects, including:

-Conducted a multi-year project to review over 30 different importing sites of a large global pharmaceutical company.
-Conducting a duty savings review of over 25 sites of a global pharmaceutical and medical device company and identified over $8m in potential savings.  
-Managed to completion a 4 year Focused Assessment for a large automotive supplier;   
-Conducted 2 joint FCPA and Trade Compliance Reviews for US and Overseas companies.
-Completed two global customs compliance reviews which included the implementation of ground-breaking process improvement projects, as well as the development and roll out of a company’s manuals at multiple global sites.
-Developed a series of global customs compliance training programs for the American Association of Exporters and Importers.

headline: Leader of Pursuit Negotiation and Pricing Team at KPMG
topSkills: Coaching • Pricing Strategy • Negotiation • Business Analytics • Financial Modeling
about:
As the leader of KPMG’s Pursuit Negotiation and Pricing group, I bring over 25 years of management consulting and business experience to my role within the firm’s Clients & Markets practice. I lead a team of senior negotiation and coaching professions who advise KPMG’s largest and most strategic business pursuits, shape and promote innovative pricing strategies, and direct complex negotiations to deliver optimal outcomes for both KPMG’s clients and the firm worldwide. I advise Account Lead Partners and work across all KPMG functions—Advisory, Tax, Audit, and Legal—ensuring negotiation and pricing strategies are tailored to client needs while sustaining profitable growth for the firm. I lead multidisciplinary teams in developing AI-enabled negotiation assets, building commercial frameworks, executing high-value deal structures, and fostering cross-functional collaboration in pursuit strategy.

My leadership in this capacity draws upon a long history in professional services delivery, with a proven track record serving leading organizations in health care; higher education; transportation; industrial manufacturing; and the technology, media & telecommunications (TMT) sectors. 

My foundational technical expertise, combined with a deep understanding of business demands, positions me to address both the challenges and opportunities presented by AI. This is a central focus of my team's efforts. 

These diverse experiences enable me to navigate the evolving landscape of professional services, drive innovation in pricing and negotiation, and deliver impactful, sustainable solutions for clients and KPMG alike.

headline: Manager, Advisory at KPMG US
about:
Greg is an experienced manager with the KPMG Health and Government Advisory Practice focusing on compliance and strategic funding in state and local government and healthcare. Greg dedicates his time and effort to understanding each client’s strategic needs and priorities, building collaborative relationships, and delivering opportune solutions. He has 15 years of experience working with public sector agencies and not-for-profits, including state healthcare departments, public and private PK-12 and higher education institutions, and other charitable organizations. 

Greg’s experience includes data governance, modeling, and visualization; policy and governance standards development for information technology and enterprise architecture; and program evaluation for compliance with contractual, legislative, and regulatory policies. Prior to KPMG, he worked at the University of Chicago and the Chicago Public Schools in various budget, analytics, and management roles. Throughout his career, he has been responsible to provide measurable evidence that outcomes are being met for multiple stakeholders and major projects supporting operations administration and budget management totaling over $1 billion in federal, state, local, and grant funding. 

Greg holds an MPA in Public Management and Public Financial Administration from Indiana University, an MBA in Global Challenges and Business Analytics from the University of Illinois, a BA in Political Science from the University of Illinois, and Certificates in Business Analytics and Project Management from the University of Chicago. He is also a certified Project Management Professional (PMP) and a member of the Project Management Institute. In addition to his work in the government and not-for-profit sector, Greg is also a member of the American Cancer Society Associate Board of Ambassadors in Chicago.

projects.title: Quinlan Ramble 2017
projects.description:
During Spring Break 2017, I had the amazing opportunity to attend the annual Quinlan Ramble with the Quinlan School of Business at Loyola University Chicago. The Ramble is an annual trip made with a few coordinators and a group of undergraduate students. On the trip, the students have a chance to visit a wide range of companies and to network with Loyola alumni. 

This year, the Quinlan Ramble visited New York City and toured an amazing assortment of companies including but not limited to the NYSE, Blackstone, Time Inc., KPMG, and Bloomberg. I found the trip to be an unforgettable experience that introduced me to a wide range of individuals and provided me with priceless advice for my career and my future. In addition, we had an amazing chance to network with a number of professionals and Loyola Alumni at an Alumni Reception hosted at the New York Athletic Club. All of the people I met and built relationships with is what really made this trip such a priceless experience. 

The Quinlan Ramble opened my eyes all kinds of work environments and really lived out the Jesuit value of learning through experience. I cannot thank the coordinators and the Quinlan School of Business enough for giving me an amazing and unforgettable way to spend my Spring Break.

experience.companyName: New York City Mayor's Office of the Chief Technology Officer
experience.description:
Abstract:

Eighteen percent of New York City residents (1.5 million people) do not have access to a
broadband connection either at home or on a mobile device. New Yorkers who lack affordable
or quality internet based on where they live face a barrier to full economic and social inclusion.
In January 2020, the New York City Mayor's Office of the Chief Technology Officer (MOCTO)
published the Internet Master Plan (IMP), which aims to make the internet affordable and
inclusive for all New York City residents by expanding broadband infrastructure and presents a
vision for universal connectivity.

To accompany future phases of the IMP, the team was asked to identify important digital equity
stakeholders in NYC who could serve as potential partners in leveraging expanded broadband
connectivity. To accomplish this, the team created a framework for identifying digital equity
stakeholders composed of four criteria areas and produced a Digital Equity Ecosystem Map — a
visualizable dataset of key stakeholders.

Through desk research and interviews, the team found that to create digital equity, the City of
New York must create healthy Digital Equity Ecosystems, made up of a broad range of
stakeholders who all play a role in facilitating digital equity, including those which address
broader societal issues.

The team makes a number of recommendations to ensure the IMP, a commendable move
toward ending the digital divide in NYC, includes efforts to ensure all individuals have the
information technology capacity and support needed for full participation in our society,
democracy, and economy.

I am an attorney and strategic advisor to corporate legal teams and elite law firms. As a veteran partner of both Big Law and the Big Four, I have an innate understanding of how lawyers work — and how they should work —as well as what tools, skills, and structures they need to thrive in high-stakes legal practices. 
My Big Law-Big Four background is as rare as it is valuable, providing insights and solutions that legal teams struggle to find elsewhere. Having practiced at the highest levels of the legal profession for over two decades, I bring a different quality of strategic insight and understanding to bear in solving the challenges legal organizations face. This experience is central to my effectiveness as an advisor, and a key reason why leading corporate legal teams and elite global law firms seek me out to define the strategies and approaches they use to tackle their most important challenges. In short, I help good legal teams become great, and great legal teams become exceptional.

Dátus Tomasovich is a Managing Director in Chicago’s State and Local Tax (SALT) Practice and serves as a local and national leader for SALT Asset Management and Family Office/Private Client services.  Previously based in NYC, Dátus helped start the firm's SALT asset management practice. He has 15 years experience serving clients in the areas of tax structuring, consulting, compliance, and financial statement audit/attestation. During his tenure, he consulted on $100B+ in transaction work covering everything from blockbuster real estate transactions, mergers/acquisitions, PE buyouts, credit, art sales, and the largest alternative energy development projects in the country. His leadership and intrepid step into an overlooked area of state taxation brought to light the infinite complexities, opportunities, and pitfalls that abound in the state and local tax asset management space. 

Professional Experience
Dátus’ current and past clients include industry leaders in banking, credit, real estate, REITs, RICs, private equity, alternative investment funds, hedge, fund of funds, investment advisors, broker-dealers, market makers, closely held companies, family office, technology companies, and alternative energy. He has provided a variety of state and local tax services to his clients; including deal structuring, consulting, compliance, planning, legislative analyses and what-if modeling, controversy and audit defense, voluntary disclosure, private letter rulings, refund claims, business restructuring, real estate transfer tax, sales and use taxability studies, technology solutions, and nexus and apportionment analyses, among others.  Dátus has extensive experience with pass-through, corporate, and personal income taxes.

Dátus'​ ability to understand the most complex organizational pass-through structures and plan for the implications to the ultimate owners is something that truly sets him apart from the pack.  As a trusted adviser to his clients, Dátus works to ensure they are thinking about the long-term strategic focus of their state and local tax function by seeking alpha and managing beta.    

Dátus consults directly with his clients, colleagues across the country, and state and local tax authorities to apprise clients on state and local tax opportunities and developments.

headline: International Tax Senior Manager at KPMG US
about:
I am a senior manager in the international tax practice of KPMG US. Based in Chicago, I lead engagements providing international tax services to a variety of clients in various industries such as distribution, financial services, manufacturing, media, real estate, and technology. I have over nine years of experience assisting clients with planning and implementing complex cross-border transactions, tax compliance matters, tax provision calculations, and operational changes. In addition to my client service role, I teach international tax courses and help with recruiting efforts at KPMG.

I hold a master’s degree in taxation from DePaul University in Chicago, and I hold a master’s degree in business administration, as well as a bachelor’s degree in accounting, from Concordia University-Wisconsin in Mequon, Wisconsin. I am a licensed Certified Public Accountant in the state of Illinois, and I am a member of the American Institute of Certified Public Accountants and the Illinois CPA Society.

In my free time, I like to run, bike, or walk along the lakefront near my home in Chicago. I also enjoy volunteering for multiple organizations, including serving as an associate board member for Navy Pier in Chicago and as a mentor to students/executive in residence at my two university alma maters.

about:
I was raised in a tri-cultured environment - born in Saudi Arabia to Indian parents who wanted to provide a better life for me in America. The blend of three strong, yet unique, cultures provided me a skill set to work in dynamic environments with different personalities, and to fully understand the needs of my teams and clients. I learned to ask thoughtful questions, to listen carefully, and to propose unique solutions.

It is precisely this idea of diversity – not only in race and gender – but also in experience, relationships, and culture that promotes strategic thinking, which in turn, drives progress.  It has been the cornerstone of my personal and professional experience.

about:
Strategic and results oriented leader with over 15 years of experience designing and implementing change in business operations as well as Finance, IT, HR, Legal, and Procurement.   

Primary expertise with global business services and shared service transformations, digital transformation and delivering operational efficiencies for the CFO/CIO/CHRO/COO including Robotic Process Automation, cost savings initiatives, and shared service implementations.  Passion for delivering enterprise-wide culture and development programs and energizingcolleagues across all levels of an organization. 

In my current role, I am Director, GBS Strategy & Transformation at KPMG US, focused on driving our strategy to mature, scale and seamlessly integrate operations into GBS by leveraging onshore, offshore, and automation delivery capabilities.

In my most recent role as Chief of Staff to the General Counsel, I set and executed departmental strategy, managed internal and external communications, and led various global initiatives that support overall business direction and culture. I bring diverse perspectives and experiences to the team, and am a passionate advocate for colleague support.

Through internships in audit, private equity, and corporate finance, as well as my role as a Teaching Assistant for a data analytics course, I’ve built a solid foundation in financial analysis, data management, and advanced Excel.

My experience includes assisting with audits, performing investment research, creating valuation models, reconciling accounts, and supporting projects that required accuracy, organization, and clear communication. I also hold certifications in Google Analytics, Revenue Operations, and other business-focused areas that reflect my commitment to learning and professional growth.

Active in leadership roles and campus organizations, I value collaboration and adaptability as much as technical skills. I look forward to taking on new challenges, continuing my learning, and working toward CPA licensure.

KPMG Ignition is an innovation lab and creative problem-solving accelerator that designs and delivers immersive experiences, utilizing design thinking, strategic intelligence, and data & analytics, to help clients explore complex business challenges and guide them to breakthrough solutions.

• Led strategic client engagements in the financial services/asset management sector, designing and facilitating high-impact workshops for C-suite executives and their teams using design thinking methodologies

• Synthesized insights in real-time to help clients navigate complex challenges, presenting compelling takeaways that influenced decision-making and strategy

• Collaborated across KPMG’s practices to bring together expertise, manage multiple stakeholders, and deliver high-quality, engaging client experiences

• Developed and mentored team members, enhancing their sector knowledge and ability to translate client challenges into impactful solutions

•	Designed and facilitated a transformative three-day workshop for 25+ executive stakeholders at a nationally ranked (top 2%) Illinois high school to define district-wide data strategy specifying where a strong use of data would have the highest impact and how to change people, processes, & technology to realize impact

•	Guided the selection and detailed planning of two pivotal pilot projects focused on enhancing student attendance and preemptively identifying at-risk students, positioning the district to proactively intervene and optimize educational outcomes for 3,800+ students

•	Led cross-functional teams of 3-6 in designing, developing, and launching new services for financial advisors; identified $15-20M in new revenue opportunities for BPO services enabling 22k+ affiliated financial advisors (across 10k+ advisory firms) to outsource back-office functions (e.g., payroll) to LPL

•	Refined innovation strategy, product portfolio strategy, and GTM strategy and led 1- to 2-month lean discovery sprints to prioritize new service opportunities based on market size, user needs, competitive landscape, internal capabilities, and legal/regulatory considerations

•	Owned viability analysis of new services, conducting thorough opportunity sizing, customer segmentation strategy, competitive analysis, pricing analysis, and financial modeling (including unit economics and pro forma P&L) to drive decisions and optimize business/operating models

•	Collaborated with service designers, UX researchers, design strategists, and product managers to launch services, navigating compliance, legal, and regulatory requirements to define pilot launch roadmaps and pilot contract agreements

Served as engagement lead on Fortune 500 clients’ most critical growth & innovation initiatives and co-led firm's business strategy discipline, including business development, recruiting, team member career growth, and project staffing. Managed day-to-day client relationships and owned project workstreams spanning business strategy, product strategy, and ethnographic research. Select client engagements:

• Digital/Physical Frontier: Led engagement with Fortune 100 apparel client to define next innovation horizon at intersection of digital & physical; designed, facilitated, and synthesized multi-day ideation workshop with 25-30 senior executives and world-renowned subject matter experts across sensory, cognitive, and behavioral neuroscience to identify & prioritize new opportunity areas and define paths forward

• Future of Mobile Apps: Led engagement with Fortune 50 logistics client to define future of mobile experience and inform product strategy for consumer-facing mobile app; designed, conducted, and synthesized immersion research & expert interviews related to cutting-edge technologies (e.g., AR/VR/XR headsets, smart home/vehicle/IoT automation, "super-apps," autonomous delivery robots, metaverse) to identify nascent consumer behaviors, attitudes, and expectations and define design principles for future digital experiences

Served as engagement lead on Fortune 500 clients’ most critical growth & innovation initiatives. Managed day-to-day client relationships and owned project workstreams spanning business strategy and research & design strategy. Select client engagements:

• Autonomous Delivery: Led client engagement with Fortune 50 logistics firm developing autonomous delivery platform with 5-year revenue projections of $500M+; facilitated pricing research with customer advisory board, defined expansion strategy by use case & market, projected 10-year demand for 50+ retailers in 90+ cities, and prioritized features of service for launch

• Design Services: Led client engagement with $2B-revenue office supplies firm considering entry into $15B graphic design services industry; analyzed offerings and business models of 30+ competitors, prioritized 50+ features to define MVP, created business model and 5-year P&L with sensitivity analysis, completed audit of 40+ required capabilities, proposed sourcing strategy for 10+ missing capabilities, and developed pilot plan with objectives, methods, and exit criteria

• Healthy Buildings: Supported Fortune 500 HVAC firm in development of digital platform for smart, healthy buildings in the wake of COVID; estimated opportunity size ($10B+), defined differentiated offering based on gaps in measurement, analysis, and control capabilities of four primary competitors, and prioritized 5+ use cases based on size and client right to win

• E-Commerce Returns: Explored paths to increased market share in e-commerce returns space for Fortune 50 logistics firm; planned, led, and synthesized ethnographic research with 40-50 merchants, consumers, and client sales team members to identify pain points & opportunity areas, presented research insights in readout to senior stakeholders, designed service concepts based on insights, facilitated workshop for concept prioritization, conducted capabilities audit, defined product roadmap, and created sales enablement materials for concepts

• Future of Investing: Explored impact of pandemic on investor attitudes & behaviors for investment management firm with $2T AUM; planned, led, and synthesized ethnographic research with 10-12 financial advisors, proposed updates to digital strategy based on new investor and advisor attitudes & behaviors, and developed thought leadership relating behavioral & societal impacts of pandemic to past historical inflection points

• Fire & Security Concepting: Developed new digital product concepts in fire & security industry for Fortune 500 HVAC firm, informed by ethnographic research with industry practitioners and subject matter experts in the US, Europe, and Asia

• Cancer Center CRM: Guided world-renowned cancer center through use case identification, prioritization, and best practices for implementation of a customer relationship management (CRM) system; facilitated research sessions with subject matter experts at leading hospitals and identified internal teams for pilot program

Served as innovation strategy consultant on Fortune 500 clients’ most critical growth & innovation initiatives. Contributed to project workstreams spanning business strategy and research & design strategy. Select client engagements:

• IT Innovation Playbook: Created new internal innovation process for Fortune 500 information technology firm to support identification, prioritization, funding, launch, and governance of new-to-world business units within the company; developed process maps, employee onboarding & educational materials, and innovation proposal templates

• Digital Investment Tools: Defined, prioritized, and prototyped new digital investment tools for $2T AUM investment management firm, informed by market analysis and ethnographic research conducted with financial advisors and employees

• Autonomous Delivery: Supported Fortune 50 logistics firm in the exploration, development, and piloting of an autonomous delivery solution; completed opportunity sizing, competitive benchmarking, financial modeling, internal capabilities audit, and initial go-to-market strategy

Operated as venture capital senior associate in venture fund of AB InBev (30+ active investments in portfolio). Typical investment of $250K to $5M in transportation & logistics and consumer goods sectors.

• Created investment thesis for technology portfolio and expanded strategy for non-alcoholic beverage portfolio, utilizing “design thinking” methodology to evaluate new market opportunities and investment targets
• Analyzed 10+ beverage categories and 150+ companies to identify 15+ investment prospects and four targets; presented four investment recommendations to investment committee, receiving approval for two investments
• Supported recommendations with detailed investment memos and financial models projecting expected returns
• Assisted legal, finance, and operations teams with diligence workstreams through deal close
• Contributed significantly to finance & strategy workstreams on high-visibility project in cannabis industry; outputs included market & industry assessments, market entry strategy, and partner/acquisition recommendations

Operated as venture capital associate in venture fund of Zebra Technologies (nine active investments in portfolio). Typical investment of $1M to $5M in retail, transportation & logistics, warehousing & manufacturing, and healthcare sectors.

•	Contributed to investment thesis for investments in artificial intelligence, automation, and analytics spaces

Enrolled in the MMM program at Northwestern University, a dual-degree program offering both an MBA from the Kellogg School of Management and an MS in Design Innovation from the Segal Design Institute. Taught & advised by world-renowned design thinking experts, including the founder of Doblin as well as partners at IDEO and Gravitytank. Candidates learn best-in-class methodologies for driving innovation through the use of design thinking tools such as user-centered research methods, creative ideation, journey-mapping, and rapid prototyping.

Worked on three-person startup under VC arm of AB InBev, disrupting core business in search of $1B idea. Solved core problem of bar owners and patrons regarding consumer desire for beer variety in smaller bars.

Worked with CIO of hedge fund and lead developer to update infrastructure and modularize trading system, increasing system robustness and ensuring future changes would be less disruptive to daily trading operations. Increased trading capabilities via Clojure interface while maintaining daily trading operations with legacy C++ code base.

Led mechanical design of R&D projects showcasing new technologies (e.g., gesture recognition, wireless charging). Collaborated primarily with hardware and software engineers and worked closely with the company's business team to ensure that our team was solving the true problems of potential clients.

Led product visualization for production engineering and ensured manufacturability for all mechanical designs.  Collaborated with key stakeholders and engineering teams at partner and client companies to flesh out design requirements and constraints.

Developed method to diversify real estate investment portfolios by co-owning properties across a wide range of geographic regions, minimizing investor risk and increasing overall liquidity of real estate market.

headline: Manager Virtual Meetings | Hockey Coach
topSkills: Leadership • Analytical Skills • Product Management • Organizational Culture • Coaching
about:
Culture is the driving force behind all successful organizations in today's world. The ability to foster a collaborative, accountable, efficient and trusting relationship with those around you is paramount to developing a sustainable connection within an organization. As a self-proclaimed culture leader, I strive to reinforce these tenants in all areas of my career and, as a result, aid others in achieving and exceeding their personal and professional goals. 

Currently I am working at KPMG U.S. as the Manager Virtual Meetings overseeing our team of Webcast Producers. Our team manages and produces over 300 events for the firm leveraging multiple streaming platforms accompanied by state-of-the-art video production and conferencing technologies for both virtual and hybrid audiences. As the team manager, my goal is to enable our producers to upskill their technical aptitude and project management capabilities, while also optimizing team processes and client support to provide the highest quality streaming productions in the industry!

I previously worked as a Product Manager at Notified, an international SaaS virtual event and webinar streaming company located in Chicago. I collaborated as part of multiple Agile scrum teams to deliver new features for the company's proprietary webcast streaming tool Studio and their virtual event platform. In addition, I researched and analyzed competitor offerings, market trends and client feedback to create requirements for future product offerings, including the implementation of AI within the platform, AWS cloud storage solutions and improved engagement and analytics tracking systems. I was also the subject matter expert for all 3rd party client integrations using SSO, restful API integrations and marketing automations such as Marketo and Eloqua, while providing Tier III support for these solutions, as needed.

I am also very involved in youth hockey as a coach in the Chicago and Milwaukee areas. I am currently the Co-Coach of the Windy City Storm 19U Girls hockey team and Head Coach of the New Trier Girls High School hockey club. I have also been a certified USA hockey official since 2008.

headline: Principal at KPMG
about:
With over 25 years of experience, I specialize in managing complex financial, regulatory, legal, and reputational risks. Currently, I serve as a Principal within KPMG’s Advisory Risk Management practice, where I oversee the review and approval of all Forensic and Financial Services Regulatory & Compliance engagements. Additionally, I lead the development and implementation of generative AI solutions, enhancing our internal teams' abilities to effectively manage evolving risk challenges. My strategic approach to AI integration was further strengthened through completing the MIT Sloan School of Management Executive Program in Artificial Intelligence: Implications for Business Strategy.

Previously, as a Senior Manager in KPMG’s Financial Risk Management practice, I directed diverse risk management and treasury projects for global clients in the energy and financial services sectors. I cultivated robust client relationships by delivering tailored services such as enterprise risk benchmarking, hedge strategy formulation, and comprehensive risk management policy design.

Before joining KPMG, I served as Director of Commodity Product Development at Sempra Energy Solutions in San Diego, California. In this role, I established strategic wholesale relationships, implemented rigorous process and contractual controls, and negotiated customized electricity and natural gas contracts across the United States.

I am a licensed attorney in the State of California and hold the Energy Risk Professional (ERP) designation from the Global Association of Risk Professionals, underscoring my specialized expertise in energy markets and comprehensive risk management disciplines.

In addition to my professional commitments, I proudly serve on the Board of Trustees at La Rabida Children's Hospital in Chicago, Illinois.

Specialties: Risk management, commodity and energy trading controls, derivative valuation, contract and MSA negotiation, commodity product development, and generative AI solutions.

experience.description: Director in KPMG’s Financial Risk Management Practice (focussing on Energy Trading and Commodity Risk Management).  I function in many roles within a broadly focused capital markets and energy risk management team assisting energy companies and financial institutions on risk management capabilities including risk management design, implementation, assessment & methodology, trading/hedging strategies and risk analytics / quantification.

experience.location: San Diego County, California, United States

Activities included coordinating with the derivative structuring, risk management and portfolio management teams to create customized retail solutions / contracts through the use of master enabling agreements and term sheets.  Product structures included complex derivatives, index and fixed prices and load following for both natural gas and electricity.	

Developed strategic wholesale relationships with national and regional counter parties.  Activities include identifying and developing trading relationships based on geographic locations and product offerings (e.g., derivative offerings), negotiating ISDA, EEI, and NAESB master agreements, drafting and reviewing special provisions and negotiating credit support documents.

headline: Retired Partner at KPMG LLP
about:
Dan served as an Audit Partner and led KPMG’s Chicago Technology, Media and Telecommunications (TMT) practice where he was responsible for driving the business results for the industry through overseeing resource allocations and driving practice-wide execution against the firm’s marketplace and operational priorities. He has over 30 years of experience advising public and privately held technology and professional services companies and has worked extensively with senior client management and audit committees to deliver exceptional client experiences.
		
Having extensive experience in leading and coordinating complex worldwide audits, Dan served as lead partner for a wide variety of technology and professional services companies throughout his career with KPMG. His clients have ranged from large multinational public companies to privately held emerging growth companies. headline: M&A Tax at KPMG US
about: Shana is an experienced Manager in the M&A Tax practice at KPMG Chicago. Prior to KPMG, she worked at Alvarez & Marsal (A&M) in the Global Transaction Tax practice for almost three years, which included a six month secondment in London where she provided tax due diligence, divestiture, tax structuring, and infrastructure advisory services to UK and European PE and strategic clients on European transactions. Prior to A&M, Shana worked at EY in the Chicago Tax practice for over four years where she coached staff, managed large compliance and provision engagements, and developed and implemented process efficiencies. Shana worked in EY’s Global Compliance and Reporting group where she provided tax provision and compliance services to public and private clients, then transitioned to the Business Tax Services - Quantitative Services group in October 2015 to provide tax planning services (e.g., R&D studies, TCAs, accounting method changes) to corporate clients while continuing to serve on the tax provision team for SEC audit clients. Shana's corporate and PE client industry experience spans consumer products/F&B, retail, manufacturing/industrials, health care, real estate, and more. Shana is passionate about recruiting and retaining talented, dynamic people to KPMG, and is actively involved in University Talent Acquisition efforts at her alma mater, the University of Illinois at Urbana-Champaign (UIUC). She previously served on the Midwest M&A Tax Social & Philanthropy Committee, Recruiting & Onboarding Committee, and Culture Committee. Shana has experience interviewing experienced hire and JD candidates while at A&M and was heavily involved in EY's Campus Recruiting efforts as a Chicago Tax Ambassador at UIUC. She looks forward to participating in any and all opportunities to recruit top talent to KPMG both on campus and experienced hires. Shana is also passionate about giving back to her community. At KPMG, she participates in volunteer opportunities throughout the year and actively supports KPMG Family For Literacy (KFFL), KPMG's non-profit. Outside of work, Shana serves on the Auxiliary Board for Big Shoulders Fund ("BSF"), a non-profit that provides educational scholarships to students from low-income households in Chicago. Shana has supported BSF through volunteering, annual donations, and more since September 2013. Shana continuously seeks new opportunities to build relationships with KPMG colleagues and outside the firm and looks forward to connecting with you.

receivedRecommendations.givenAt: July 3, 2016, Michael managed Elizabeth directly
receivedRecommendations.description:
Elizabeth is an undeniably exceptional young woman, both in intellectual prowess and in personal character.

An in-class activity in my economics course at Jones College Prep required Elizabeth and her peers to read and interpret a series of data sets regarding the impact of foreign-born players on the NBA. I began the activity with a disclaimer that the data being used was part of a 37 page senior thesis from Haverford College that contained fairly advanced calculus that I had removed from the activity because it was not essential to the concepts we were addressing regarding workforce composition. After the activity, Elizabeth asked if she could have my copy of the original document to read independently, to see the calculus and all of the conclusions presented by the research, and bought it back the next class to discuss with me. This kind of independent ambition was on top of a senior year course load that included 3 Advanced Placement courses, the college admissions process, and a battery of scholarship applications. Such are the character and capacity of Elizabeth Madrigal, and this anecdote perfectly illustrates why she carries my utmost respect, as well as why any organization would do incredibly well to bring her onto their team.

projects.title: Cloud Computing Security
projects.associatedWith: Associated with Illinois Institute of Technology
projects.description:
In 2006, the word “cloud” was used by Google’s CEO Eric Schmidt to describe the business
model for providing services across the internet. Cloud computing can be defined as utilizing the
internet to provide technology enabled services to the people and organizations. It is a pool of
virtualized computer resources, based on which the Cloud Computing paradigm allows workloads to be
deployed and scaled-out .General example of cloud services is Google apps, provided by Google and
Microsoft SharePoint. It has a focus on maximizing effectiveness of the shared assets.
The boom in cloud computing has brought lots of security challenges for the consumers and
service providers. Some of these include sensitive data access, data segregation, privacy, authentication,
bug exploitation, recovery, accountability, account control. Multi located data storage and services (i.e.,
applications) in the Cloud make privacy issues even worse. Lack of proper security control policy and
weakness in safeguard lead to many vulnerabilities in cloud computing.
The security threats have become obstacles in the rapid adaptability of the cloud computing
paradigm. Significant efforts have been made to build a secure cloud computing environments and
infrastructures.
This study aims to identify the most vulnerable security threats in cloud computing, which will
enable both end users and vendors to know about the key security threats associated with cloud
computing. This project  summarizes reliability, availability, and security issues for cloud
computing (RAS issues), and proposed feasible and available solutions for some of them.

Dean's Honor Scholarships are merit-based scholarships offered to approximately 100 incoming first-time freshmen applicants by the Office of Undergraduate Admission. honorsAndAwards.title: Altman Scholar | The Altman Program in International Studies and Business
honorsAndAwards.description: The Altman Program in International Studies & Business is a special four-year undergraduate program that integrates liberal arts and business disciplines, extensive language instruction, and two study abroad experiences. Altman Scholars earn two degrees - a B.A. from the School of Liberal Arts and a B.S.M. from the A. B. Freeman School of Business. Altman Scholars specialize in a region of the world in which their chosen foreign language is spoken, and will be able to combine practical and theoretical knowledge of global economies with deep cultural and linguistic competency. The integration of a broad liberal arts education with a practical business degree will allow Altman Scholars to succeed in diverse career paths including international business, finance, marketing, politics, law, diplomacy, public health, consulting, and/or the non-profit world. This challenging dual-degree curriculum provides students with a broad liberal arts perspective and a practical business education that will enable them to be successful in a variety of career paths.

publications.title: The Cost-Benefit Analysis of the U.S. Conversion from GAAP to IFRS
publications.description:
Abstract:
This research paper is designed to explore the costs and benefits regarding the effects of the United States switching from the U.S. Generally Accepted Accounting Principles to the International Financial Reporting Standards. The beginning of the paper will explain specific aspects of each the domestic standards and international standards along with some of the main differences between the two. Research will, then, advance further into exploring the benefits of convergence on international trade, taxes, and investing. The influence of world trade in today’s business transactions will be examined as well. The costs of this conversion will then be analyzed using evidence from when other countries had made the switch to require IFRS. Throughout this paper, it should be made clear whether the benefits of switching to IFRS from U.S. GAAP outweigh the costs.

headline: International Tax
about:
As a managing director in KPMG’s Chicago International Tax practice, I bring over 12 years of experience in providing tax consulting services to both public and privately held clients. I joined KPMG in 2021, having previously spent over five years at the Chicago office of Ernst & Young LLP, where I specialized in cross-border tax advisory, structuring, compliance, and provision review for multinational clients.

In my professional and industry experience, I advise multinational companies on all aspects of global tax positions, including the tax implications of cross-border acquisitions, financing transactions, corporate restructurings, and other corporate activities. My practice also encompasses advising clients on international transfer pricing and controversy matters related to global operations, investments, and transactions. Additionally, I have supported clients in operational matters within their tax departments.

I have in-house experience from my time at Illinois Tool Works Inc., where I worked in the tax department. There, I gained a broad range of experience assisting the company with legal drafting, treasury matters, provision review, compliance assistance, and the implementation of tax planning initiatives. I have also explained and presented topics such as IRC 965 and calculation mechanics to PCAOB officials and have been a speaker at a Tax Executives Institute event, KPMG’s client events and KPMG Morning Brew, discussing various international tax topics.

My representative experience includes assisting clients with complex tax matters, such as transactional tax cost assessment and the reporting of acquisitions and divestitures. While I specialize in tax consulting related to international taxes, I also provide provision review and tax return assistance. I have performed integration tax assistance in over 55 countries and have managed several compliance engagements of varying sizes, from Fortune 200 companies to privately held firms. My current and past clients include leaders in the retail, life sciences, private equity, real estate and manufacturing industries.

about:
I am an experienced Industrial/Organizational Psychology practitioner passionate about helping organizations improve their overall employee experience and create more innovative and effective work environments. My expertise lies in the execution of projects that collect, analyze and effectively integrate people insights into an organization's strategic decision-making processes. Simply put, I help organizational leaders understand and action on the complex data around their most pressing people problems. 

To be more specific, my experience is inclusive of the entire employee survey life-cycle; from survey/assessment design and project management/administration, results analysis and delivery to management, all the way through setting effective action plans and integration of insights into strategic planning. However, my professional aim has always been to build strong partnerships with leadership and key stakeholders to ensure successful project implementation, accurately diagnose critical people issues (either overt or covert), and then leverage the most up-to-date organizational science perspectives to help organizations find the best solutions to seemingly ambiguous and complex people-related business problems.

Throughout my career, I've made every effort to help my clients think more strategically about one of the most important aspects of their organizations - their people. So, I'll end this summary with this question - organizations always conduct as much research and analysis on customer, product, and marketplace trends as they can... why not do as much when looking to understand your own employees?

experience.location: New York, New York, United States

experience.description:
• Deliver actionable insights from employee engagement survey results, informing senior executives’ people strategy and future survey administrations, while also providing guidance in existing action planning initiatives.
• Conduct external benchmarking analyses on engagement survey data, aligning current and future organizational performance with industry standards.
• Rethink future employee listening initiatives through the investigation and alignment of organizational needs (e.g., dashboards, survey versioning) with current market-leading survey vendor capabilities.
• Lead the redesign of the employee engagement survey using evidence-based practices such as advanced psychometric techniques and leveraging deep experience in the construction of effective employee listening surveys.  
• Develop and implement an in-person focus group program designed to provide deeper qualitative insights into data-driven opportunity areas across different business verticals.

As a Principal consultant in Mercer's Employee Research Practice, I served as project owner, strategic advisor and team leader for all projects within my portfolio. I sought to bring the best value to all of my client engagements, incorporating the most up-to-date people science approaches to implementing employee survey work, analyzing complex data, and providing sound strategic people-related business recommendations. My approach to project execution included, but was not limited to, what I considered the three most important tasks as a thought leader and project owner:

- Help clients align and execute their vision for employee listening projects with key organizational initiatives and/or to investigate gaps in data coverage. 
- Delivery of data-based, dynamic, and engaging insights to leadership teams and/or key stakeholders, used to help identify clear and meaningful organizational strengths and where interventions were needed. 
- Provide best-in-class service in terms of project execution, from thoughtful and detailed initial planning, all the way through results delivery and actioning.

During my senior consultant time, it was necessary for me to display an expert level of knowledge and delivery efficiency across the entire breadth of the client project lifecycle, inclusive of all products and tools (e.g., engagement surveys, onboarding/exit, 360, culture assessment, M&A integration surveys, total rewards preferences assessment). 

Outside of further sharpening the KSAOs cultivated and refined in the intern and junior consultant levels (i.e., generating insights, data analyses, deliverable creation, and project management), this was the period were I spent the most time developing my ability to design specific projects to meet client demands, creating and defining my own unique client management and presenting style, and connecting our employee survey work with broader strategic initiatives across existing and potential clients. 

In short, I became the sole owner of a wide range of projects and sales opportunities across many different industries and organization-types, building my overall client portfolio, and helping to ensure the execution and overall value of all projects.

Upon promotion from the intern level, my new duties as a consultant included the ownership of all deliverables before they were passed to senior consultants/principals for presentation and debrief with clients. 

Key developmental aspects in this period included the refinement of my ability to make meaningful connections across data to provide key insights for clients, relieving senior consultants of the task and creating a more efficient and stream-lined process that cut down on lead time to results delivery. I also enhanced my proficiency in data analysis to the point where I was able to be the sole owner of data sets, from initial cleaning through analysis for presentation. 

The connection between these two developmental stages was key in my next promotion, where an expert level of intimacy with the data was required to not only pull out the most valuable and impactful insights for my clients, but also to solidify my own standing as an SME to the clients I was tasked with working.

As a consulting intern, my key business priorities included supporting junior and senior consultants in foundational tasks such deliverable creation and quality assurance. This is where I developed my skills in terms of detail orientation, time management, and initial analysis and summarization of key project outcomes. Additionally, a large portion of time was spent training and refining my skills in terms of overall data analysis techniques, including, but not limited to, writing syntax in SPSS, cleaning data, and producing finalized data sets for consultant-led presentations.

publications.title: Empirically Examining Demographic Differences Through the Lens of Remote Work
publications.description: As organizations weigh the costs and benefits of remote work in the post-pandemic era, some researchers have proposed that remote work may be especially beneficial for certain marginalized groups. However, empirical data on this topic remains scarce. Therefore, the purpose of this research is to empirically identify potential diversity, equity, and inclusion implications of remote work. Specifically, we examined employee freedom from harassment and discrimination across various demographics and remote work status. Significant main effects were found for workers with disabilities as well as for remote vs fully on-site. Male remote workers experienced a greater increase in freedom from harassment than did female remote workers. Additionally, remote workers perceived lower upward mobility potential in their jobs, while receiving higher performance ratings, as compared to their non-remote counterparts.

publications.title: Was Remote Work More Challenging for Women? A Field Study
publications.publishedAt: The Society for Industrial and Organizational Psychology (SIOP) Conference 2021 · Apr 15, 2021
publications.description: During the pandemic, many organizations implemented remote work arrangements. These accommodations may have caused some employees—particularly women—to feel isolated and overwhelmed. This study was conducted to understand the challenges that remote employees experienced during the pandemic. Using survey data, we explored the extent to which male and female employees felt balanced, supported, and able to cope with demands. Results reveal a number of gender-based differences.

publications.title: Is Engagement Different for Tenure, Ethnicity, and Gender Across Industries?
publications.publishedAt: The Society for Industrial and Organizational Psychology (SIOP) Conference 2018 · Apr 1, 2018
publications.description:
Woo, V. A., Amato, F., & McGuire, M. S. (2018, April). Is engagement different for tenure, ethnicity, and gender across industries? Poster presented at the Society for Industrial and Organizational Psychology (SIOP) Conference, Chicago, IL.

We examined employee engagement across five industries (98 companies, over 3 million employees) by tenure, ethnicity, and gender. There were significant main effects for industry, tenure, and ethnicity; as well as significant interaction effects for industry by all three demographic variables.

publications.title: Business Transformation and the Corporate Agenda
publications.description: Trends affecting business transformation are unprecedented in their sheer number and intensity. For corporations, change has become the new normal, according to a KPMG study of more than 900 senior executives from U.S.-based multinationals and asset managers, as well as one-on-one interviews with top executives. Business transformation has taken hold across the broad corporate landscape due to the confluence of several important triggers, including a tipping point in globalization, a major slowdown in Western economies, significant shifts in technology and energy costs, and the challenges of regulatory compliance.

publications.title: Business Transformation and the Regulatory Environment
publications.description:
The current dynamic regulatory environment is a very important trigger of transformation. Depending on the industry sector, the regulatory environment can be a partial or dominant trigger for transformation. Regulatory compliance, though a necessity spearheaded by external factors, is an opportunity to transform and catapult a company to a new level of competitive advantage. In this paper, we outline three different approaches that companies currently employ, depending on the industry, the regulations and/or the companies’ approaches to incorporating them.

New regulations often demand complex changes, but also create a big opportunity to spearhead changes in other areas of business for those companies that are able to gain a proactive view of the current and upcoming regulatory landscape. Regulatory vigilance—including regulatory elements as part of business transformation—leads to increased acuity about transformation processes. Research shows that companies that integrate regulatory issues in the transformation framework are more likely to assess their operating models against business strategy and follow better practices regarding the processes and structuring of their transformations.

publications.title: Business Transformation: People. Process. Results
publications.description:
Business transformation has taken hold across the broad corporate landscape due to the confluence of several important triggers, including a tipping point in globalization, a major slowdown in Western economies, significant shifts in technology and energy costs, and the challenges of regulatory compliance.

The key to the success of a business transformation is often in the organizational approach. Characteristics of innovative approaches to transformation include:
• Having a formal process for prioritizing business transformation initiatives
• Using a combination of an executive committee and a working team to prioritize transformation initiatives
• Handling transformation in a centralized, top-down manner 
• Having a dedicated internal organization to handle transformation

publications.title: From Burden to Competitive Advantage: Regulatory Change and Transformation in Financial Services
publications.description:
For companies in the financial services sector, the challenges of the current global regulatory environment are twofold: Regulations are expensive to implement, and they can limit revenue growth and profitability. Thus, to gain competitive advantage through a transformation, financial services firms need to design strategy and an operating model based on a regulatory framework.

Linking how you’re addressing regulatory issues along with the business strategy is incredibly important. That is a differentiator for the financial services firms that get transformation right. In this paper, we address three important steps that need to be taken to achieve a successful regulatory transformation.

publications.title: WEBCAST: Business Transformation and the Corporate Agenda
publications.description: This January 2014 webcast explores the types of business transformations being undertaken by companies today and the confluence of factors that triggered them. It also discusses how executives and thought leaders approach the strategy and execution of a business transformation in their organizations.

headline: Change, Communications & Organizational Decision Systems | Turning Internal Alignment Into Infrastructure
about:
I work at the intersection of organizational decision systems and enterprise communications—where alignment becomes infrastructure.

Organizations don’t fail because of bad ideas—they fail because internal decisions are made without clarity, accountability, or alignment. After more than 14 years working across complex enterprise transformations, one pattern has become impossible to ignore: communication is treated as an output, when in reality it is the final stage of a decision system few organizations understand, let alone govern.

I study how messages, approvals, and cross-functional decisions move inside organizations—and how those internal choices determine external realities. My work focuses on the frameworks, governance models, and decision paths that shape what companies say before they say it. Whether the context is a strategic announcement, a policy change, or a leadership transition, communication isn't just what is written—it’s what is decided.

Selected Impact

• Turned around a failing transformation initiative for a Fortune 1 client by establishing decision governance, alignment frameworks, and accountability structures—directly resulting in extended engagement and successful implementation.

• Built and deployed cross-functional visibility systems inside a major consulting practice that exposed hidden decision bottlenecks and increased identifiable execution opportunities by 60%, later replicated across multiple business units.

Focus Areas

Organizational Decision Systems | Communication Governance | Executive Alignment | Enterprise Change Architecture

Principles I Operate By

Seek clarity. Make decisions visible. Align before acting. Build systems that scale behavior.
